metadata.title: TMUA 2019 · Paper 1
metadata.description: Worked steps, progressive hints and reviewed follow-up questions.

matches.rationale: Uses the axis and a repeated intercept to identify a quadratic’s coefficients; reinforces vertex information as algebraic constraints.
Tracks the input coordinate of a quadratic minimum under scaling and translation, retaining the sign of the vertex shift.
Finds the parameter-dependent quadratic vertex and uses its coordinates to identify the feasible graph movement.
Equates a line and parabola and uses the discriminant to decide intersection or tangency. The same threshold calculation now allows equality.
Eliminates one variable to obtain a quadratic and requires a strictly positive discriminant for every allowed parameter.

Both use the discriminant to enforce the requested real-root behaviour while preserving the stated parameter domain. The candidate’s leading coefficient is explicitly nonzero and the exceptional discriminant-zero value gives a repeated root.
The required coefficient is a sum of selected binomial coefficients; adds the contributing terms without expanding the whole product.
Targets one coefficient through two binomial selections. It rehearses identifying and combining only contributing choices, but has no arithmetic-series sum.
Selects low-degree terms of nested powers and a product; targets coefficient extraction and adding contributions, not summing a sequence of expansions.
A derivative recurrence repeatedly multiplies one monomial by a constant. It rehearses finding a closed pattern and indexing it, rather than repeated square roots.
Evaluating a definite integral turns a recurrence into a fixed multiplier. This develops recognition of a repeated operation and the correct power count.
Direct equal-length GP block comparison: subtraction isolates a later block, and the position shift determines the power of the common ratio.

Prerequisite transfer: recover a geometric ratio from the power of that ratio connecting indexed terms. The candidate then sums a convergent infinite progression; it does not practise the original comparison of two equal-length term blocks.
sharedKnowledge: GP term indices determine powers of the ratio
recover a ratio from supplied term information

matches.rationale: Sum and sum-of-squares conditions determine GP ratios. It reinforces geometric sums and admissibility, but not the direct equal-block comparison.
Uses centre distance and both radii to calculate the separation of disjoint circle boundaries.
Perpendicular radii at a common internal tangent yield the right-triangle constraint between two circles.
The distance from the centre to the y-axis equals the radius at tangency; translates a geometric contact condition into coefficients.
Direct analogue: differentiation at a prescribed input produces a quadratic in a parameter, which is minimised.
The tangent slope becomes a parameter quadratic; its minimum controls the maximum normal gradient through a reciprocal.

Integration produces a quadratic in a parameter and completing the square minimises it. It targets the second optimisation stage, using integration rather than differentiation to obtain the quadratic.

Prerequisite transfer: both compare trapezium approximations with exact area. The original transports a known finite-partition error under transformations and does not establish a global curvature sign. The candidate classifies trapezium error by comparing chord position after translating and reflecting a parabola.

Prerequisite transfer: the original transports a known finite-partition error under transformations without establishing a global curvature sign; the candidate separately tests a sufficient second-derivative condition for trapezium error.
Finds intersections of a line and a cubic, uses lobe symmetry, and integrates the difference to determine the parameter.
Opposite-side lobe areas become signed integrals with the correct roots as bounds; equal areas combine into a zero integral.
Recovers unsigned component areas from overlapping signed integrals. It reinforces correctly combining lobes, but the integrals are supplied instead of evaluated.
Splits at the zeros of a parabola to distinguish signed integrals from total unsigned area.
sharedKnowledge: Split absolute values at their zeros

matches.rationale: Both resolve an absolute value into polynomial pieces before integration. The candidate adds even symmetry and unsigned enclosed area; the original retains the signs of a definite integral over an asymmetric interval.
Distinguishes signed and absolute integrals, then uses the input reflection in f(|x|); forces careful separation of the two meanings of a modulus.
sharedKnowledge: Split absolute values at their zeros

matches.rationale: A logarithmic system is converted into simultaneous algebra, with domain checks before accepting the roots.
Linearises a mixed logarithmic-exponential system and retains positivity of exponentials when solving the parameter condition.
A logarithmic substitution produces a polynomial and its solutions must be converted back to the original variable before calculating the requested difference.
Simplifies a rational derivative into powers, integrates, and uses an initial point to fix the constant.
sharedKnowledge: Fit the additive constant from an initial value

matches.rationale: A radical quotient is rewritten as powers before integration, avoiding an unnecessary quotient-integration approach.
sharedKnowledge: Rewrite a radical quotient as powers
Evaluate an antiderivative at specified inputs

matches.rationale: The candidate isolates the original integration stage by integrating fractional and negative powers and evaluating the definite bounds. It does not rehearse simplifying a rate or fitting an initial value.
An exponential substitution gives a positive quadratic denominator whose attainable minimum controls a reciprocal maximum.
Completes the square in 2^x and checks that the quadratic vertex lies in the positive exponential range.

The shared prerequisite is expressing a quadratic in completed-square form and reasoning about its maximum. The candidate constrains that maximum through a parameter; it has no inner-function substitution or trigonometric range, so those should not be described as shared methods.
Reduces an equation involving sine and cosine, locates all permitted quadrants, and selects the final solution in the full interval.
A quadratic in absolute cosine requires admissible root selection and counting all angles, including the interval endpoints.
Square-root branches combine with a tripled angular interval; directly reinforces updating the angle domain before counting solutions.

The candidate becomes a quadratic in 2^(2x), giving positive exponential values that are converted back with logarithms. Both questions require a common-base hidden variable, admissibility checks and recovery of the original roots.
Converts mixed powers of 3 into a quadratic, then uses logarithm laws to sum the original roots.
A common-base exponential substitution produces a quadratic and the result requested is a sum of logarithmic roots.
Moves integral limits under an input translation and adds the rectangle contributed by a vertical translation.
Expresses the integral of a vertical translate using the original signed area and a constant rectangle.
Builds requested integrals from unit intervals, including reversed bounds; rehearses signed additivity without needing the unknown function.
Direct trigonometric product sign-chart analogue, with different factors and strict endpoints.
Direct sine/cosine product inequality with inclusive factor zeros; requires both same-sign cases.
Intersects two trigonometric sign intervals and measures their total accepted length as a fraction of the domain.
Finds a curve contact point from a specified normal, requiring the negative reciprocal gradient and matching the line equation.

Prerequisite transfer: formulate a geometric distance using both coordinates and find an attainable minimum. The candidate minimises the squared distance of a moving vertex; it does not practise the original parallel-tangent and perpendicular-segment construction. The retained normal-line questions supply that geometric prerequisite.
sharedKnowledge: form a distance from both coordinate differences
minimise a nonnegative distance expression and check attainment

matches.rationale: Builds a normal from the derivative, finds its axis intercepts, and uses Pythagoras to calculate the segment length.
A trigonometric sequence has a repeated six-term block with zero sum; the remainder of the term count determines the partial sum.
Complementary trigonometric terms pair to a constant sum. It develops exact term counting and cancellation structure, using symmetry rather than a repeating cycle.
A recurrence produces repeated pairs whose sums simplify a long series. It rehearses grouping and term counts without trigonometric functions.
Direct cubic root-count problem: the two stationary heights must straddle zero strictly to obtain three distinct real roots.
Derives the parameter range for a cubic’s root count from stationary heights, then recognises a sufficient subrange.
Uses stationary heights and monotonic intervals to count distinct roots of a quartic; transfers the same graph-counting method to one higher degree.

review.method: Compare demanded solution steps against original question crops and official worked solutions. All follow-ups come from another year or the early specimen. Exact reprints are excluded.

coverageNotes.note: No three other official repeated-square-root exponent-halving questions were identified. The three follow-ups explicitly target recognition, closed forms and index tracking in recurrences, with different repeated operations; these are transfers, not exact analogues.
The binomial-coefficient sum has one close coefficient-summation follow-up and two targeted coefficient-selection transfers; arithmetic summation is recapped in the original hints.
One close periodic trigonometric partial-sum match; the other two rehearse cancellation/grouping and careful term counts using complementary angles or recurrence pairs.
